strings.name: Mary Robinson
strings.role: Former Irish president · Human rights and climate justice advocate
strings.summary: Robinson moved from law, Senate service and rights litigation into national leadership, becoming Ireland’s first woman president in 1990 and UN human rights commissioner in 1997–2002. She links climate change with poverty, gender and vulnerable people’s rights. Former Elders chair, she stepped down in 2024. Elected in 2026 to lead GGGI’s Assembly and Council, she is due to begin the 2027 term after this dossier’s cutoff.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Former Irish president and UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, she has long advanced climate justice and protection of vulnerable people’s rights.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: President and rights commissioner
strings.highlights.h1.text: Served as Irish president and UN human rights commissioner, advancing rights and public participation.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Legal education at Trinity College Dublin and King’s Inns; Harvard LLM (1968).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Climate justice advocacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Connects climate policy with poverty, gender equality and vulnerable people’s rights in international advocacy.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Elected to GGGI leadership
strings.timeline.t1.text: Elected Assembly President and Council Chair for 2027–2028; not yet in office at cutoff.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Leaves Elders chairship
strings.timeline.t2.text: Santos succeeded her; she remained an active member.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Chairs The Elders
strings.timeline.t3.text: Succeeded Kofi Annan, leading work on peace, rights and global public issues.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Climate Justice Foundation
strings.timeline.t4.text: Established a rights-centred climate and development initiative, leading it until 2019.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Founding Elder
strings.timeline.t5.text: Joined the international public-figures group initiated by Mandela.
strings.timeline.t6.title: UN human rights commissioner
strings.timeline.t6.text: Left the presidency to hold the UN office until 2002.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Irish president
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became the first woman to hold Ireland’s presidency.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Senator and professor
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered the Senate for Dublin University and became a Trinity law professor.
